subject: The Duergar Invisibility Practice
fact: Duergar merchants and individuals in Gracklstugh routinely use their innate ability to turn invisible, which is so common that it is treated as mundane, yet its misuse in commerce creates distrust and confusion among outsiders.
source_quote: The Duergar can become invisible at will; you never know who is watching. ... A merchant suddenly turns invisible during a transaction but keeps speaking as if nothing has happened.

subject: The Duergar Merchants’ Paradox
fact: Multiple Duergar merchants in the Blade Bazaar behave irrationally: some turn invisible mid-transaction and deny it, others claim to speak to non-existent brothers, and prices shift arbitrarily, suggesting a widespread psychological or magical malaise infecting the city’s commerce.
source_quote: A merchant suddenly turns invisible during a transaction but keeps speaking as if nothing has happened. ... another weapons merchant threatens a customer, and when the customer protests, the merchant denies ever saying so. ... a cloth merchant suddenly stops mid-negotiating and starts talking to someone he refers to as his brother. ... 'His brother doesn’t exist.'

subject: The Duergar Slave Trade
fact: The Duergar of Gracklstugh operate a systematic slave trade, capturing and selling prisoners in Gracklstugh, which is confirmed by Jimjar and later reinforced by the discovery of captured individuals on the keelboat.
source_quote: Jimjar shouts, 'You know what the Duergar do for a living?' ... 'Yes, they capture slaves that they sell in Gracklstugh.'

subject: The Mad Giant's Breakthrough

source_quote: The rhythmic hammering of the city’s forges is drowned for a second by a thundering roar and the sound of crumbling rock. Duergar and visitors alike turn to look as a two-headed, gray-skinned giant burst through a gate, howling madly and lashing out left and right, littering the plaza with rock and stone debris. As he bellows, one of his swings connects with a duergar soldier, whose broken body flies through the air and crashes near you with a sickening crunch.

subject: The Magical Item Negotiation

subject: The Second Sundering Reference

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a Duergar metropolis in the Underdark where order and labor are prized over art and beauty, with plain, functional buildings, smelters, and forges creating an atmosphere of a vast work camp, and acrid smoke that burns the sense of smell.
source_quote: The buildings are plain and functional. Whereas the Drow would have decorated their homes with etchings and art, the walls of the Duergar homes are plain. And the ambiance is just that of work. The sound of hammers warping metals, the stench and heat, and the light of the smelters make all of Gracklstugh appear as one large work camp. But the acrid smoke makes breathing hard and burns through his sense of smell, which he will remember most from his time here.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a massive Duergar metropolis in the Underdark, characterized by oppressive industry, invisible agents, deceptive merchants, and pervasive madness; its Blade Bazaar is a chaotic marketplace where truth is fluid and survival depends on navigating illusions and shifting loyalties.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the Duergar metropolis in this part of the Underdark.
source_quote: the metropolis of the Duergar in this part of the Underdark

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: The acrid smoke in Gracklstugh burns through Daz’s sense of smell.
source_quote: the acrid smoke makes breathing hard and burns through his sense of smell

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: The buildings in Gracklstugh are plain and functional, lacking art and opulence.
source_quote: the buildings are plain and functional... the walls of the Duergar homes are plain

subject: Gracklstugh ambiance
fact: Gracklstugh appears as one large work camp, with the sound of hammers, stench and heat, and the light of smelters.
source_quote: The buildings are plain and functional... the sound of hammers warping metals, the stench and heat, and the light of the smelters make all of Gracklstugh appear as one large work camp.

subject: Gracklstugh City Gates
fact: The gates separating the Darklake District from the rest of Gracklstugh are a physical and symbolic barrier, through which a two-headed giant later bursts, shattering the illusion of order and unleashing chaos.
source_quote: The gates at the end of the road keep the Darklake District isolated from the rest of the city. ... a two-headed, gray-skinned giant burst through a gate, howling madly and lashing out left and right...

subject: Gracklstugh walls
fact: The walls of Duergar homes are plain, unlike the etchings and art of Drow homes.
source_quote: Whereas the Drow would have decorated their homes with etchings and art, the walls of the Duergar homes are plain.

subject: Kuotoan Boat
fact: The Kuotoan Boat is a vessel where the party’s former castaways debate who should interrogate the captured Duergar prisoner, with Sarith recommending Daz due to his methods.
source_quote: He can hear the debate on the Kuotoan boat about who should question their Duergar prisoner. ... Sarith explains, 'The Lolth’s guards trained me. I am an expert, but having seen Daz’s approach, I recommend that he be given the first crack at extracting information.'

subject: Lost Tomb of Khem
fact: The Lost Tomb of Khem is a destination referenced by Sethir as the group’s next objective after acquiring equipment in Gracklstugh, where they intend to find treasure.
source_quote: Sethir mutters, 'We plan to get equipment and then go to the Lost Tomb of Khem, where we will find treasure!'

subject: The Caverns Near Gracklstugh
fact: The caverns near Gracklstugh are referenced by Buppido as his bolt hole, where he intended to return to praise the Divine Plan, suggesting a hidden network of refuge spaces outside the city’s control.
source_quote: I just wanted to return to my bolt hole in the caverns near the city and praise the Divine Plan.

subject: Underdark journey
fact: The long journey through the dark waters of the Underdark has led them to Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The long journey through the dark waters of the Underdark has led him here to the metropolis of the Duergar in this part of the Underdark.

subject: Duergar

subject: Duergar invisibility
fact: The Duergar can become invisible for a whole hour.
source_quote: Hemeth laughs, "Yes, that would be a good thing to worry about. The Duergar can become invisible for a whole hour." And he turns invisible.

He thinks there might be some rivalry between the Duergar gods and the Dwarven gods, but then he remembers something he read: that religious conflict is not always what it seems. The Dwarves and the Duergar compete for the same resources, and political conflict may matter more than any religious principle or dogma. 'This is not the will of any god. This is the will of the people,' he mutters.

subject: Grygum

source_quote: Yes, it’s Duergar Keelboat. You can see the crates." ... "He finds some gold and a jug that he learns later can be used to generate any liquid.

subject: Duergar Keelboat
fact: The abandoned boat is identified as a Duergar Keelboat.
source_quote: Yes, it’s Duergar Keelboat. You can see the crates.

subject: Dulgir's mace
fact: Grygum purchases a mace from merchant Dulgir after the merchant shifts to speaking with a Baldurian patriar tone.
source_quote: Grygum... asks if he wants to buy or sell. "Sell this mace?"... the Duergar suddenly shifts, speaking with the stilted tongue of a Baldurian patriar... He is the proud owner of a new mace.

subject: Eldritch Claw Tattoo
fact: An Eldritch Claw Tattoo can be purchased in Gracklstugh but not in the Darklake District.
source_quote: Zalthir has been thinking about some magical items he wants and was disappointed when Hemeth said that magical goods could be purchased in Gracklstugh but not in the Darklake District.

subject: Eldritch Claw Tattoo
fact: An uncommon magical item sought by Zalthir, which can be purchased in Gracklstugh but not in the Darklake District, and is obtainable through Brannam Redmarch’s contacts.
source_quote: Zalthir asks them, 'Can either of you get me Eldritch Claw Tattoo?' ... Brannam lights up, 'Yes! I know a guy. But it will take a few days.'

subject: Eldritch Claw Tattoo
fact: An uncommon magical item sought by Zalthir; it is rumored to enhance combat prowess with arcane claws and is obtainable only through Brannum’s underground contacts, representing the group’s need for magical upgrades to survive Gracklstugh’s dangers.

subject: gold
fact: Zalthir finds gold in the Duergar Keelboat’s casks and chest.
source_quote: He finds some gold

subject: holy symbol
fact: Grygum uses his holy symbol to channel Bahamut's power against the giant.
source_quote: pointing his holy symbol at the mad giant who burns with necrotic damage and the power of Bahamut.

subject: Jug of Any Liquid
fact: A jug found in the Duergar keelboat that can generate any liquid, and the first liquid generated is mayonnaise, which enhances the taste of bland food such as mushrooms.
source_quote: He finds some gold and a jug that he learns later can be used to generate any liquid. The first liquid they generate is mayonnaise. After eating bland mushrooms, mayonnaise will make anything taste much better.

subject: Jug of Any Liquid
fact: A magical jug found on the Duergar keelboat that can generate any liquid; the first liquid produced was mayonnaise, which dramatically improves the taste of bland food and becomes a symbol of small comforts in a hostile world.

subject: jug of liquid generation
fact: The jug found in the keelboat can generate any liquid, and the first liquid generated was mayonnaise.
source_quote: He finds some gold and a jug that he learns later can be used to generate any liquid. The first liquid they generate is mayonnaise.

subject: jug that generates liquid
fact: Zalthir finds a jug that can generate any liquid.
source_quote: a jug that he learns later can be used to generate any liquid.

subject: mace
fact: Grygum purchases a mace from Dulgir.
source_quote: A few minutes later, he is the proud owner of a new mace.

subject: Tongue of Madness
fact: The Tongue of Madness is a magical mushroom that forces consumption and compels truth-telling, revealing hidden thoughts, resentments, and delusions; it was used on Buppido to extract confessions and expose the psychological fragility of the party.

subject: Tongue of Madness
fact: The Tongue of Madness is a magical mushroom that, when eaten, compels the consumer to speak their true thoughts and opinions, revealing hidden animosities and secrets.
source_quote: Zalthir hands him a mushroom, The Tongue of Madness, and says, 'Eat.' And Buppido does and starts talking. 'I just wanted to return to my bolt hole in the caverns near the city and praise the Divine Plan.' And then he starts expressing his true opinions of his companions: 'You all have been so annoying. Daz has foul-smelling breath. Thorin thinks his muscles are impressive. Eldeth is -not- interested in him.'

subject: Tongue of Madness
fact: The Tongue of Madness is a mushroom that, when eaten, forces the consumer to reveal true thoughts.
source_quote: Zalthir hands him a mushroom, The Tongue of Madness, and says, "Eat." And Buppido does and starts talking.

subject: Buppido’s Divine Plan
fact: Buppido’s obsession with the Divine Plan and his sudden clarity after consuming the Tongue of Madness suggest he was manipulated or deluded by an external force; his true allegiance and the nature of the 'plan' remain unresolved.

subject: list of names
fact: The list of names Zalthir found might be worth looking into.
source_quote: Grygum shrugs. “I think they might be worth looking into.”

subject: madness in the city
fact: Grygum believes some madness afflicts the city, possibly similar to what consumed the Kuo-toans.
source_quote: The answer disturbs Grygum, who is convinced that some madness afflicts the city, perhaps the same madness that consumed the Kuotoans.

subject: nature of the giant
fact: Thorin observes that stone giants never talk or bellow, suggesting the giant is unnatural.
source_quote: Thorin, who overhears the giant, shouts, “Stone giants never talk. And they certainly don’t bellow. Something is wrong.”

subject: Origin of Gracklstugh’s Madness
fact: The source of the city’s collective delusions—whether magical, divine, or psionic—is unknown; Grygum suspects it is not religious but political, while Zalthir and Jimjar wonder if it is tied to the Time of Trouble or a lingering artifact of the Second Sundering.

subject: teachings of Bahamut
fact: Grygum remembers the teachings of Bahamut that when you do a good turn for someone, they may do a good turn for you.
source_quote: And then he remembers the teachings of Bahamut that when you do a good turn for someone, they may do a good turn for you.

subject: The Invisible Brother
fact: Multiple merchants claim to speak to an invisible brother who does not exist; this recurring delusion may be a symptom of the city’s corruption, a magical illusion cast by Duergar enforcers, or a sign of deeper planar intrusion.
